goal.statement: Hold p99 on the four shapes that dominate time (the daily report, email lookup, campaign funnel and account timeline) at 8 and 32 sessions, with no other shape worse than today, at the lowest-cost tier that does it.

interval.method: distribution-free binomial order-statistic interval (normal approximation), pocbench.stats.quantile_ci

latency_basis.definition: client-measured latency of each successful query minus the median probe (SELECT 1) round trip of the same run
latency_basis.invalid_run: discarded and re-run; never scored, never averaged in
latency_basis.name: net latency
latency_basis.why: runner-to-Neon round trip varied 3.5-66 ms across jobs (R9)

noise_rule.then: comparisons against that baseline are inconclusive (not met)

method.pooling: percentiles are computed on observations pooled across the repetitions of one configuration, level and cache state
method.slice: held_out (the loop never sees it; ADR 0002, R3)
method.spread: every criterion also reports the per-repetition values and their spread, (max - min) / median

under_sampled.rule: a percentile is supported when the pooled observations and the distinct instances beyond it reach the floors (load model, ADR 0018). An unsupported percentile in a ceiling criterion makes it unsupported (not met). A no-regression comparison uses the highest percentile supported on both sides, falling back p99, p95, p50

verdicts.ceiling: met if the interval's upper bound <= ceiling; failed if its lower bound > ceiling; otherwise inconclusive (not met)
verdicts.cost_ceiling: pooled CU x cu_hour_usd x measured seconds / 3600 / successful queries
verdicts.mix_level: mix-level numbers are reported, never scored (R12)
verdicts.no_regression: met if candidate upper bound <= (1 + tolerance) x baseline upper bound; failed if candidate lower bound > (1 + tolerance) x baseline upper bound; otherwise inconclusive (not met)
verdicts.recommendation: every criterion met; otherwise the candidate fails and the output may be a refusal (ADR 0011)
verdicts.throughput_floor: median across repetitions of successful queries per second

profile_reference.note: profile latencies are the naive capture's client latency; they describe today, they are not the criteria
